video_title: "We're Worried About 2027" - Stocks To Plunge 30%? | Chance Finucane @OxbowAdvisors
gist: Oxbow Advisors CIO Chance Finucane outlines a defensive Q4 outlook: AI stocks look overvalued and 2027 could bring a 30%+ stock decline from slowing growth and inflation, so Oxbow holds mostly non-AI quality stocks, short Treasuries, and actively trimmed gold and energy positions.

insights.claim: Oxbow is pretty concerned about 2027 and would not be surprised by a 30%+ stock market decline, with its directional data only covering roughly the first 8 months of 2027.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Defensive positioning ahead of a possible H1 2027 drawdown, with buying opportunities in H2.
insights.quote: I don't think we would be surprised if it the stock market went down 30% or more.

insights.claim: Oxbow's framework: the worst stock environment is slowing real growth combined with slowing inflation, driven by tough year-over-year comparisons; H1 2026 saw accelerating growth (cycling the spring 2025 tariff shock) and an inflation spike (oil jump from the war), so 2027 faces steep comps and slowing nominal GDP.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Slowing nominal GDP historically hurts cyclicals and tech; markets may price it 3 months ahead rather than the usual 1.

insights.claim: Oxbow thinks the Fed is too optimistic about 2027 growth; the firm expects a difficult first half.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Fed-versus-Oxbow forecast gap is a source of downside surprise risk.

insights.claim: A chart of the record gap between trailing (10-year Shiller) PE and forward PE is at its highest in 35+ years; when that gap rolls over after long uninterrupted growth, a significant bear market has historically followed, while a compressed gap marked buying opportunities like the early 2000s and 2009.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Valuation signal says focus on risk, not on buying; the market is far from a compressed-gap buy zone.

insights.claim: Oxbow aims to limit losses to less than half of any 30% stock drop so it can think opportunistically rather than defensively, and plans to trim January winners to be right-sized for a rough first half of 2027.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Capital preservation creates the optionality to buy near a low.
insights.quote: we want to make sure that we are allocated properly heading into that.

insights.claim: Ted Oakley's approach is to break out the 'Ferrari' only after roughly a 50% market decline (1974, 2003, 2009 cited), when many cheap assets can double or triple; for now Oxbow drives the durable 'SUV'.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Aggressive risk-taking is reserved for deep-bear lows, which are far away now.

insights.claim: About 30 AI-beneficiary stocks make up roughly half of S&P 500 market cap, and the majority of S&P stocks are down at least 20% from highs, so the market is split into two halves moving oppositely.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Index highs mask weak breadth; AI concentration is the main index risk.

insights.claim: Oxbow sees roughly 30% downside for tech and about 50% for semiconductors, making AI names too risky to add or hold meaningfully.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Avoid AI beneficiary valuation risk; downside outweighs upside.

insights.claim: Memory semiconductors, the DRAM ETF and the Korean stock index all peaked in June, made a lower high in September's rally, and are down about 40% from highs; semiconductors fell 16% over eight sessions.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Lower-high pattern in AI-related cyclicals is a warning sign.

insights.claim: Semiconductors and AI beneficiaries are cyclical businesses, and slowing growth plus slowing inflation is consistently a bad backdrop for tech stocks, which Oxbow expects for at least half of 2027.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Cyclical exposure should be reduced into the expected slowdown.

insights.claim: October AI pullbacks did not drag the index because money rotated into non-AI stocks, signaling that investors remain broadly bullish and wanting full equity exposure, which Oxbow reads as a sign of elevated exuberance.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Rotation rather than exit suggests sentiment is still stretched.

insights.claim: Oxbow holds just over 2% of its stock strategy in AI beneficiaries: Texas Instruments and ASML (each under 1%), Fortinet (halved after doubling in about six months) and Zoom (partly for its Anthropic stake).
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Shows concrete minimal AI exposure with lower-volatility names.

insights.claim: Construction spending is growing over 70% annually in data centers and about 10% in power, while every other sector (residential, manufacturing) is down year over year; any slowdown in data center build-out financing could by itself slow the economy.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Economy and market both hinge on AI capex continuing.

insights.claim: Oxbow thinks the Fed under Kevin Warsh may wait longer to intervene but would still step in during a truly bad market, because so much household savings sits in the S&P 500.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Fed put may be delayed, not removed, implying a deeper drawdown before support.

insights.claim: A research service estimates the positive wealth effect from rising stock portfolios had triple the long-term-average impact on consumer spending this year, so a market reversal would hit consumption hard.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Equity declines feed directly into economic slowdown via spending.

insights.claim: Oxbow is incrementally adding to 2-3 year Treasuries as yields approach 5%, but will not go beyond three years because it believes that since 2020 yields are in a rising, volatile regime.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Short duration locks in 4-5% while avoiding rising-yield duration risk.

insights.claim: Short-term Treasuries at 4-5% provide a base rate with minimal downside that lets investors wait comfortably for better opportunities and reduces drawdown risk and emotional decision-making.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Higher yields make wealth preservation easier than during the zero-rate decade.

insights.claim: Muni bonds should be judged on tax-adjusted yield and the spread to same-maturity Treasuries; the spread recently got abnormally wide and Oxbow filled client muni needs in shorter maturities, expecting spread compression.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Monitor muni-Treasury spread for entry points; use experts.

insights.claim: After three-plus years of strong returns (about 14-15% S&P this year after roughly 20% average in prior years), Adam Tagert argues mean reversion makes de-risking prudent.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Streak of strong years raises odds of a mean-reverting year.
insights.quote: it's like seeing somebody roll, you know, seven several times in a row at the craps table.

insights.claim: Ted Oakley's forthcoming book 'Asleep at the Wheel' (byline 'you own too much stock for your age') targets over-65 investors with outsized equity weights after a 17-year run; a 50% decline requires a double to recover, which older investors may lack time for.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Older cohorts hold the most equity and face the most sequence risk.
insights.quote: you own too much stock for your age

insights.claim: Oxbow cut its precious metals weight in High Income from about 15% to 6-7% in January, re-added to about 12% in July after a pullback (gold roughly $4,000 to $4,700; miners up ~50%), then sold silver and a silver miner as the rally fizzled to a lower high with gold near $4,100.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Example of dynamic sizing around a sector it remains long-term bullish on.

insights.claim: Oxbow keeps core precious metal holdings (gold bullion, Agnico Eagle Mines, royalty companies) and trims the most volatile positions, and treats gold between 3,800 and 4,200 as a good price while planning for a break below.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Hold quality core, trade the periphery.

insights.claim: Oxbow runs roughly half of each commodity sleeve as stable core and half as dynamically managed; an example was National Energy Services Reunited, bought at 22, half sold at 35, rest sold slightly below cost, still netting a gain versus holding.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Active trimming of winners converts round trips into gains.

insights.claim: Secular bull markets of ~20 years are followed by 10-16 year rangebound periods (2000-2013, late 1960s-1982) where index buy-and-hold goes nowhere, so Oxbow expects returns may require actively shifting among stocks, metals and bonds.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: A new rangebound regime would favor active allocation over passive indexing.

insights.claim: XLE is up over 50% year to date, about double the next-best sector (tech), and energy remains Oxbow's favorite sector, though it hit about 20% of High Income and was trimmed by selling uranium, coal and Transocean.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Energy was the standout 2026 sector; Oxbow is harvesting risk.

insights.claim: In 2022 energy stocks rose over 60% on an oil spike and then went nowhere for three years; Oxbow is watching for a repeat and may pull back to core pipelines over the next six months, noting slower growth and lower inflation is difficult for energy.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Energy may stall once the Gulf-driven oil spike fades.

insights.claim: About half of Oxbow's energy allocation is pipelines with stable cash flow and dividends that it holds without active shifting, while producers and periphery names are managed dynamically.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Midstream is the stable anchor in energy.

insights.claim: Oxbow's stock screen requires strong, consistently growing free cash flow (growth in 8-10 of 10 years, e.g., Visa or Mastercard with 10-15% growth) at valuations judged relative to each sector's own history, with commodity businesses the exception.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Sector-relative valuation across diversified quality names.

insights.claim: Recent stock additions include energy, healthcare, real estate services businesses sold off on AI-disruption fears, and two small high-quality bank positions; the minimum account is $2 million.
insights.speaker: Chance Finucane, Oxbow Advisors CIO
insights.so_what: Shows where non-AI value is being sought.
